steps: Learn the key vocabulary for places in town and local area
Master hay for existence and estar for location of a specific place
Use se puede + infinitive to say what you can do in your area
Give balanced opinions using lo mejor es que and lo peor es que
Build sentences about your ideal city using the conditional tendría / habría
method_card.title: My Town and Local Area
method_card.content:
This lesson covers places in your town or village and how to describe what you can do there. You will use hay for existence and se puede + infinitive for general statements about what can be done.

SpanishEnglish
la ciudadthe city
el pueblothe village / small town
el barriothe neighbourhood
el centro de la ciudadthe town centre
el parquethe park
el mercadothe market
la bibliotecathe library
el ayuntamientothe town hall
la piscinathe swimming pool
el polideportivothe sports centre
haythere is / there are
se puede + infinitiveyou can / one can
lo mejor es quethe best thing is that
lo peor es quethe worst thing is that

Grammar focus — Hay vs Estar: Use hay for existence: Hay una piscina en mi barrio (There is a swimming pool in my neighbourhood). Use está / están for the location of a specific, known item: La piscina está cerca del parque (The swimming pool is near the park). NEVER use hay with a definite article: say hay una piscina, never hay la piscina.

Se puede + infinitive is the impersonal way to say what can be done in a place: Se puede nadar (you can swim), Se puede ir de compras (you can go shopping). The negative is No se puede hacer mucho (You can't do much).

Model paragraph: Vivo en un pueblo pequeño. Hay un parque, una biblioteca y muchas tiendas. Lo mejor es que es tranquilo, pero lo peor es que no hay cine. Mi ciudad ideal tendría un polideportivo y más restaurantes. (I live in a small village. There is a park, a library, and many shops. The best thing is that it is quiet, but the worst thing is that there is no cinema. My ideal city would have a sports centre and more restaurants.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — town descriptions appear across all papers each year

steps: Learn the key vocabulary for shops, clothing and shopping transactions
Master the three-way demonstrative system: este (here), ese (there), aquel (over there)
Use quisiera and me gustaría for polite requests when shopping
Practise asking about prices, sizes and availability
Build a full shop role-play combining all four skills
method_card.title: Shopping and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers shopping vocabulary, prices, sizes and polite requests. You will practise asking for items and using the three-way Spanish demonstrative system.

SpanishEnglish
ir de comprasto go shopping
el centro comercialthe shopping centre
la tiendathe shop
el mercadothe market
¿cuánto cuesta?how much does it cost?
caro / barataexpensive / cheap
en oferta / en rebajason offer / in the sales
la tallathe (clothing) size
el númerothe shoe size
quisieraI would like (polite)
me gustaríaI would like (polite)
este/estathis (near speaker)
ese/esathat (near listener)
aquel/aquellathat over there (far from both) (Higher)

Grammar focus — Three-way demonstratives: Spanish has THREE levels of distance, unlike English which only has two (this / that). Este/esta/estos/estas = this/these (close to the speaker — este jersey). Ese/esa/esos/esas = that/those (close to the listener — ese abrigo). Aquel/aquella/aquellos/aquellas = that/those over there (far from both — aquel sombrero). All demonstratives agree with the noun in gender and number.

Model paragraph: Quisiera comprar este jersey azul, por favor. ¿Cuánto cuesta? Esa blusa también me gusta, pero es un poco cara. ¿Tiene una talla más grande? (I would like to buy this blue jumper, please. How much does it cost? I also like that blouse, but it is a bit expensive. Do you have a bigger size?)

exam_context.frequency: Core transactional topic — shop settings appear frequently in the speaking exam role play

gold.source_text: I would like to buy this green dress and those shoes over there. How much do they cost? I think that jacket over there is too expensive, but these trousers are on offer.

Check: three-way demonstrative system (este/ese/aquel) with correct gender agreement, quisiera/me gustaría, cuánto cuestan (plural), price adjective agreement (cara agrees with chaqueta). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

wrong.Quiero: Quiero is the present tense (I want). For a polite request, use the conditional querría, me gustaría, or quisiera.

gaps.correct_explain: Querría is the yo conditional of querer (I would like/want). Me gustaría or quisiera are also accepted — all are polite conditional forms.

wrong.puede: puede is the third-person present. The subject here is 'I' and we need the subjunctive pueda.
wrong.puedo: puedo is the present indicative. After para que, use the subjunctive pueda.

gaps.correct_explain: pueda is the present subjunctive of poder (to be able). Para que (so that) is always followed by the subjunctive in Spanish.

method_card.title: Transport and Getting Around
method_card.content:
This lesson covers transport vocabulary, comparatives and describing journeys. You will learn to say how you travel and compare different modes of transport using más/menos ... que.

SpanishEnglish
en cocheby car
en trenby train
en autobúsby bus
en aviónby plane
en barcoby boat
en biciby bike
en metroby underground
a pieon foot
rápido / lentofast / slow
caro / baratoexpensive / cheap
cómodocomfortable
mejor que / peor quebetter than / worse than
la estación de trenthe train station
el andénthe platform (Higher)

Grammar focus — Comparatives: Use más ... que (more/faster than), menos ... que (less/cheaper than), and tan ... como (as ... as). Irregular comparatives: bueno → mejor (better), malo → peor (worse). Always use que (not de) for 'than': El tren es más rápido que el autobús. Adjectives in comparisons must still agree with the noun: La bici es más barata que el coche (feminine, agrees with bici).

Model paragraph: Prefiero viajar en tren porque es más rápido que el autobús y más cómodo que el coche. Sin embargo, es más caro. Ir en bici es mejor para el medio ambiente y menos estresante que el metro. (I prefer to travel by train because it is faster than the bus and more comfortable than the car. However, it is more expensive. Going by bike is better for the environment and less stressful than the underground.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — transport comparisons and train station role-plays appear regularly

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive of poder after si

wrong.puedo: puedo is the present tense. After si in a hypothetical, use the imperfect subjunctive pudiera.
wrong.podr\u00eda: podría is the conditional. In Spanish, the conditional goes in the MAIN clause, not after si.

gaps.rule: Conditional of viajar (yo) in main clause

wrong.viajo: viajo is the present. The main clause of a hypothetical si sentence needs the conditional.
wrong.viaj\u00e9: viajé is the preterite. This is a hypothetical, not a past event.

gaps.correct_explain: viajaría is the yo conditional of viajar — 'I would travel'. The main clause of a si + subjunctive sentence uses the conditional.

wrong.es: es is the present tense. The sentence is hypothetical → use the conditional sería.
wrong.era: era is the imperfect (it was). This is not about the past.

gaps.correct_explain: sería is the conditional of ser — 'it would be'. Used in the main clause of a hypothetical sentence.

method_card.title: The Natural World and Environment
method_card.content:
This lesson covers the natural world, environmental problems and solutions. You will use obligation phrases and the future tense to discuss what must be done to protect our planet.

SpanishEnglish
el medio ambientethe environment
la contaminaciónpollution
el cambio climáticoclimate change
el calentamiento globalglobal warming
los residuos / la basurawaste / rubbish
el reciclaje / reciclarrecycling / to recycle
ahorrar energía / aguato save energy / water
plantar árbolesto plant trees
las energías renovablesrenewable energy
sostenible / ecológicosustainable / ecological
el bosque / la selvathe forest / the jungle
el río / el lagothe river / the lake
la montaña / la costathe mountain / the coast
hay que + infinitiveit is necessary to / we must

Grammar focus — Obligation phrases and the future tense: Use these impersonal obligation structures: hay que + infinitive (it is necessary to — strongest, impersonal), se debe + infinitive (one must), deberíamos + infinitive (we should — polite conditional), es importante + infinitive (it is important to). The simple future tense is formed by adding endings to the infinitive: reciclaré, usaremos. Irregular future stems: hacer → har-, poder → podr-, tener → tendr-. Example: En el futuro usaremos energías renovables (In the future we will use renewable energy).

Model paragraph: Hago todo lo posible para proteger el medio ambiente. Reciclo, no malgasto agua y voy en bici al instituto. Deberíamos usar menos plástico. En el futuro usaremos más energías renovables y habrá menos contaminación. (I do everything possible to protect the environment. I recycle, I don't waste water and I go to school by bike. We should use less plastic. In the future we will use more renewable energy and there will be less pollution.)

exam_context.frequency: Popular topic in the writing and speaking exams — especially at higher tier

Check: obligation phrases (hay que/se debe/deberíamos + infinitive — no extra preposition before infinitive), future tense (infinitive + ending, not present), superlative structure (el/la más + adjective), accents (deberíamos, habrá, reciclaré). Be encouraging but specific. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific suggestion"}
